title: Sentence Completion
lines: Sentence completion is the largest verbal item type in USAT, with about six questions. A sentence has one or two blanks, and you choose the word or words that fit best. Some items test vocabulary in context; others test grammar: tense, auxiliary verbs, prepositions, articles and agreement. In every case the sentence itself contains the clue.
## Step by step
- Read the whole sentence before looking at the options.
- Find the clue words that tell you what the blank must mean.
- Predict a word of your own, then pick the option closest to it.
- Read the finished sentence again. It should make sense and be grammatical.
## Context clues
| Clue | Signal words | What it tells you
| Contrast | but, although, however, yet, despite, while | the blank goes against another part of the sentence
| Support | and, also, moreover, in addition | the blank continues the same idea
| Cause and result | because, since, so, therefore, as a result | the blank follows logically from a reason
| Definition or example | that is, such as, for example, a colon | the blank is explained nearby
> Although the medicine was ______, the patient refused to take it.
> (A) bitter  (B) effective  (C) costly  (D) unpleasant
> "Although" signals contrast: the patient refused something good. Effective fits, B. Bitter and unpleasant would be reasons to refuse, so they remove the contrast.
## Two-blank items

Work with the blank that has the stronger clue first, and cross out every option whose word fails there. Then test the survivors in the other blank. Both words must fit; a pair with one perfect word and one wrong word is still wrong.
> The new manager was so ______ that even small decisions took her weeks, and her team grew ______.
> (A) decisive … content  (B) hesitant … impatient  (C) careless … proud  (D) quick … bored
> Decisions taking weeks shows a hesitant manager, and a team kept waiting grows impatient: B.
## Grammar for blanks
- Tense: match time words. "By next June, she ______ her degree" needs the future perfect: will have completed. "Since 2019" usually needs the present perfect: has lived.

- Conditionals: If + present, will + verb (If it rains, we will stay in). If + past, would + verb (If I had time, I would help). If + past perfect, would have + past participle (If he had studied, he would have passed).
- Subject and verb agree: "Each of the students has a book." "Neither the teacher nor the pupils were late" (the verb agrees with the nearer subject).
- Auxiliaries and modals: after can, could, must, should, will and would, use the base verb (must go, not must to go). "Used to" for past habit takes the base verb (I used to walk).
- Gerund or infinitive: enjoy, avoid, finish and suggest take -ing (avoid wasting); want, decide, hope and agree take to + verb (decided to leave).
- Articles: "an" before a vowel sound (an hour, an MBA), "a" before a consonant sound (a university, a one-rupee coin).
## Prepositions often tested
| Correct use | Common error
| good at, interested in, afraid of | good in, interested on
| depend on, insist on, consist of | depend upon is fine; consist from is wrong
| accused of, charged with | accused for
| married to, similar to, different from | married with
| on Monday, in June, at 5 o'clock | in Monday
| prefer tea to coffee | prefer tea than coffee
> The committee insisted ______ a full report before it would approve the funds.
> (A) for  (B) on  (C) at  (D) to
> The verb insist takes on: insisted on a full report, B.
## Traps to avoid
! Do not choose the hardest word because it sounds impressive. The right word is the one that fits the clue.
! Watch negatives: "not", "hardly" and "rarely" reverse the meaning. "The plan was hardly a ______" needs a positive word, such as success.
! A word can fit the meaning and still fail the grammar. "She is capable ______" needs of + -ing: capable of managing.
## Quick check
- Find the signal word: contrast, support, cause or definition.
- Predict before you look at the options.
- In two blanks, use the easier blank to eliminate first.
- Check tense, agreement, verb pattern and preposition before you choose.
